title: Alma Redemptoris Mater
hookLine: the Marian antiphon of Advent and Christmas
last: BEHOLD THY MOTHER: MARY MOTHERS EVERY DISCIPLE.

lines: NIGHT PRAYER ENDS WITH A SONG TO MARY.
cards: When the Church's night prayer is finished, there's one more thing before the silence: a short song to Mary, called an antiphon. Which one depends on the time of year, the way a coat does.
In Advent, the dark weeks of waiting before Christmas, and on through the Christmas season, it's this one. It opens with three Latin words that climb slowly, like steps: Alma Redemptoris Mater.
Loving mother of the Redeemer. Tradition credits it to a monk, Hermann of Reichenau. Over the next few days the night song changes with the seasons, and i'll follow it around the year with you.

teach.h: GATE OF HEAVEN, STAR OF THE SEA.
teach.b: Take it a phrase at a time. First, two pictures. It calls Mary the open gate of heaven, and stella maris, star of the sea.
On a dark sea, sailors could steer by a star that stayed put while everything else moved. Advent is a season of waiting for light, and the song gives the people waiting a fixed point to steer by.
Then the request, and it's honest. In Latin: succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo.

teach.h: HELP THE ONES FALLING, TRYING TO RISE.
teach.b: Help the people who are falling, who are trying to get up. Not a people who have it together. A people in the middle of falling, still trying to rise.
Then the wonder. While nature marveled, natura mirante, she gave birth to her own holy Creator. A mother holding the one who made her.
Nature doesn't explain it; nature marvels. That's Christmas, said in a single breath. Last, the song goes back to the start of the story.
It remembers her taking that Ave from Gabriel's mouth, the angel's greeting in Luke's Gospel, which the Douay-Rheims gives as "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee."

teach.h: HAIL, FULL OF GRACE, THE LORD IS WITH THEE.
teach.b: Then it ends where a long day often ends, asking for mercy: peccatorum miserere, have mercy on sinners. Gate, star, falling and rising, wonder, mercy. A whole season, folded small enough to sing before bed.

how: Catholics who pray the Liturgy of the Hours close Night Prayer with an antiphon to Mary; in Advent and the Christmas season it is traditionally the Alma Redemptoris Mater, often sung in Latin chant in monasteries and some parishes.

games.q: you're writing a night song for people waiting in the dark of Advent. who do you ask Mary to help?
o: a people who have it all together.
a people falling, still trying to rise.
only the ones who've already arrived.
games.why: the antiphon asks: succurre cadenti, surgere qui curat, populo. help the people who are falling, who are trying to get up.

practice: If you can, play a recording of the Alma Redemptoris Mater in chant and let your attention ride the melody like a small boat on a long wave; you don't need the Latin.
If you can't, say a few phrases slowly, one per breath: loving mother of the Redeemer, gate of heaven, star of the sea, help the ones who fall and try to rise.
If you pray, let it be your prayer; if not, let it be music in the dark.
